definition: Hygiene factors are cleanliness-related conditions or behaviors, such as a child’s hand hygiene, that can affect exposure to infectious agents. In this study context, poorer hand hygiene strengthened the harmful effect of low parental contact with sick people on type 1 diabetes risk.

reasons: The packet does not define “hygiene factors” as “cleanliness-related conditions or behaviors,” nor does it explicitly state that they affect exposure to infectious agents.

The packet only provides a specific study finding involving “Lower child hand hygiene” and its interaction with parental occupational social contact; it does not support the more general framing in the definition.

The definition’s final sentence adds a broader causal wording (“harmful effect of low parental contact with sick people on type 1 diabetes risk”)—the packet reports the interaction and synergy index, but the exact phrasing and causal characterization are not directly supported beyond that interaction description.

The packet supports only a study-specific child hand-hygiene measure and its interaction with parental occupational contact; it does not define “hygiene factors” generally as cleanliness-related conditions or behaviors.

The claim that these factors “can affect exposure to infectious agents” is broader than the packet, which reports an association with type 1 diabetes risk and an interaction with enteroviral indices, not a general exposure definition.
